title: Oregon's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Oregon's 2nd Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Cliff Bentz against Democratic nominee Chris Beck. The district encompasses over 70,000 square miles across 20 counties in eastern and southern Oregon and has been held by a Republican since 1981; it is the only Oregon congressional district with more registered Republicans than Democrats. Bentz, who won the 2024 general election with 64% of the vote, is heavily favored in this safely Republican district according to nonpartisan election forecasters such as the Cook Political Report. Beck, a former state representative and Obama administration official, advances after winning a competitive six-candidate Democratic primary and is campaigning on rural healthcare access, affordability, and land conservation.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in Oregon's 2nd Congressional District as of June 2026. Nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report) rate the race as 'Solid Republican.'

candidates.name: Cliff Bentz
candidates.summary: Cliff Bentz is the Republican incumbent representing Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A third-generation Oregonian raised on family cattle ranches in Harney County, he is an attorney who specialized in ranch reorganizations and water law before entering politics. Bentz previously served in the Oregon House of Representatives and Oregon State Senate, and he handily won the 2026 Republican primary with nearly 80% of the vote against two challengers.

candidates.name: Chris Beck
candidates.summary: Chris Beck is the Democratic nominee for Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, a former state representative who served three terms in the Oregon House from 1997 to 2003 representing the 12th District. He later worked as a rural policy advisor in the Obama administration at the U.S. Department of Agriculture and as a conservation professional with the Trust for Public Land. Beck won a six-candidate Democratic primary with 34% of the vote in May 2026 and faces incumbent Cliff Bentz in the general election, campaigning on rural healthcare access, affordability, and land use planning.
